agent.name: Promethean Technology Classification Agent
agent.specialty: Broad technological significance (incremental / breakthrough / potentially Promethean) and its bounded weight in a present application decision

analytical_question: Is agentic AI incremental, a breakthrough, or potentially Promethean on present evidence, and how much should that broad significance influence this organization's present decision about the specified application?
general_et_finding: Classification: Breakthrough | Potential-Promethean candidacy: UNRESOLVED | Floor confidence: Moderate | Ceiling confidence: Low. Layer 1: agentic AI is a usable, deployed system: an LLM that directs its own process and tool use, unlike a fixed workflow (E15), offered commercially and connected to tools through a shared protocol supported by major AI products (E14). It is evaluated as that system. The course timeline's 'Potential Promethean ?' label for generative AI (C1, slide 20) is not inherited. Barrier statement: Before this technology, carrying out a multi-step task across digital systems (finding information, operating software, completing a transaction) required a person to perform or directly drive each step; this was not experienced as a limitation but as the definition of clerical and professional knowledge work. Suppression test (present tense, dependence evidence only): if agentic AI vanished today, the old state would largely return. Generative AI as a whole assisted only about 1-5% of US work hours in late 2024 (E6); agents are used by a minority even of developers (31%, E13); Danish earnings and hours show precise null effects two years after ChatGPT (E9); and many enterprise agent projects are still pilots, with over 40% forecast to be cancelled (E12). Dependence is forming in software development and AI tooling (E13, E14), but no evidence shows that removal would collapse dependent systems. Result: dissolution in progress, not yet testable. On present evidence this is a reduction, so the classification is capped at Breakthrough (C1). Breakthrough floor: independent evaluations show an order-of-magnitude capability change within one tier, economic activity. Computer-use agent accuracy rose from about 5% to 66.3% in one year, still below a 72.35% human baseline (E5), and task horizons have doubled roughly every seven months (E4). Layer 3, prospective (cannot raise the classification): 10X - Supported for capability, Unknown in the field (the best agent completed 30% of realistic workplace tasks, E11); widespread impact - Partial: broad potential exposure (E3) but small realized effects (E6, E9, E10); paradigm shift - Partial: software that chooses its own steps (E15), so far inside existing work designs; catalytic effect - Partial and early: a shared protocol ecosystem, self-reported (E14); democratizing effect - Partial: largest gains for novices in an assisted setting (E7); irreversibility - Unknown, verifiable only after the fact (C1). Tiers: one observed (economic activity). Cognitive and social life is exposed but not yet shown reorganizing around agents. Mode: not Confirmed; candidacy unresolved. This paragraph is identical for every organization at this evidence date (2026-10-18).
application_finding: Baseline: counselors, public admissions channels and an existing public chatbot, Violet (E17), whose design is not disclosed. The proposal adds multi-step clarification and a permission-limited appointment request inside approved content and staff approval. It does not sit on the frontier where the broad barrier would be dissolved: staff remain the accountable channel, and switching the tool off returns the existing process. It is a reduction of handling effort within an existing process. Application significance: Incremental, consistent with Assignment 3's sustaining process-innovation finding (C3). Because Violet already exists, the decisive comparison is Violet or simple retrieval versus the proposed agent, not staff versus agent. Evidence from an assisted support setting (E7: +14% on average, +34% for novices) is relevant to the application's possible value but says nothing about Promethean status.
organization_specific_finding: Significance weight on the present decision: Low. The broad classification may shape three things: (a) monitoring cadence (a semiannual refresh of capability and dependence evidence); (b) modest learning investment in agent evaluation, approved-content governance and permissions design; and (c) avoiding long vendor lock-in while the ceiling is unresolved. Incremental-counterfactual test. PASS: the matched comparison from Assignment 3 (staff-only, Violet or simple retrieval, proposed agent, on the same approved tasks) is worth doing even if agentic AI were merely incremental. CONDITIONAL: a live applicant-facing pilot passes only if that comparison shows better cost per correctly completed task at acceptable consequential-error rates. FAIL: a multi-year platform commitment, staffing reductions or autonomous record changes, because their justification would rest on Promethean expectations rather than application evidence. The moderate fast-follower posture affects timing (SPS can learn from peer evidence and needs no first-mover premium) but not the classification. Management should be confident that the technology matters, and should not let that importance stand in for application evidence. Hype-invariance: the memo's claims change none of the above (see contrary_evidence_or_limitations).

evidence.claim: Course instrument: Layer 1 system test; barrier statement; suppression test ('if the old state would simply return ... at most a breakthrough'); six criteria; single tier = breakthrough; irreversibility verifiable only after the fact; Confirmed vs Potential mode.
evidence.source_or_reference: [C1] Andres Fortino, ET Promethean Technologies FA26, slides 8-10, 15-17, 19-20 (user-supplied course material)
evidence.notes: Framework only. The slide-20 label for generative AI is an exemplar, not evidence about agentic AI.

evidence.claim: Agents dynamically direct their own processes and tool use; workflows follow predefined code paths; agents trade latency and cost for performance and risk compounding errors.
evidence.notes: Definition used for Layer 1; not evidence of superiority.

evidence.claim: More than 10,000 active public MCP servers and 97M+ monthly SDK downloads; protocol donated to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation, co-founded by Anthropic, Block and OpenAI.
evidence.notes: Self-reported counts. Early catalytic signal; not dependence or value.

evidence.claim: Nearly 40% of US adults 18-64 use generative AI, but it assists only 1-5% of all work hours, with time savings of about 1.4% of work hours.
evidence.source_or_reference: [E6] Bick, Blandin, Deming, The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI, NBER WP 32966; Management Science 2026. https://www.nber.org/papers/w32966
evidence.notes: Fast adoption is diffusion context; the hours share is dependence evidence. Generative AI broadly, not agents.

evidence.claim: 31% of developers currently use AI agents, 17% plan to, 38% do not plan to; 46% distrust the accuracy of AI output.
evidence.source_or_reference: [E13] Stack Overflow 2025 Developer Survey press release. https://stackoverflow.co/company/press/archive/stack-overflow-2025-developer-survey/
evidence.notes: Developers are the leading domain; minority use is not dependence.

evidence.claim: Precise null effects on earnings and recorded hours; effects larger than 2% ruled out two years after ChatGPT's launch.
evidence.notes: Denmark; chatbots, not agents; short run.

evidence.claim: Over 40% of agentic AI projects forecast to be cancelled by end-2027; only about 130 of thousands of 'agentic AI' vendors judged real.
evidence.notes: A forecast, used only as a caution against hype, not as proof of failure.

evidence.claim: Computer-use agent accuracy (OSWorld) rose from about 5% in 2024 to 66.3% in 2025, below a 72.35% human baseline.
evidence.source_or_reference: [E5] Stanford HAI, The 2026 AI Index Report. https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2026-ai-index-report
evidence.notes: Benchmark, not production reliability. The same report's investment and adoption-speed figures are not used as significance evidence.

evidence.claim: Frontier 50% task-completion time horizon about 50 minutes in early 2025, doubling roughly every seven months since 2019.
evidence.source_or_reference: [E4] Kwa et al. (METR), Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks, arXiv 2503.14499. https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14499
evidence.notes: Software tasks; extrapolation is a projection.

evidence.claim: About 80% of US workers could have at least 10% of tasks affected and about 19% at least 50%; LLMs show general-purpose-technology traits.
evidence.source_or_reference: [E3] Eloundou, Manning, Mishkin, Rock, arXiv 2303.10130; Science 2024. https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.10130
evidence.notes: Potential exposure only; authors partly OpenAI-affiliated.

evidence.claim: The most competitive agent completed 30% of simulated workplace tasks autonomously; long-horizon tasks remain beyond current systems.
evidence.source_or_reference: [E11] Xu et al., TheAgentCompany, arXiv 2412.14161; NeurIPS 2025. https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14161

evidence.claim: Experienced open-source developers took 19% longer with early-2025 AI tools while believing they were 20% faster.
evidence.source_or_reference: [E8] Becker, Rush, Barnes, Rein (METR), arXiv 2507.09089. https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09089

evidence.claim: Task-based estimate: total-factor-productivity gain no more than 0.66% over 10 years, adjusted below 0.53%.
evidence.source_or_reference: [E10] Acemoglu, The Simple Macroeconomics of AI, Economic Policy 40(121) 2025. https://www.nber.org/papers/w32487

evidence.claim: Electrification's productivity gains arrived only after factories were reorganized, after a long lag.
evidence.source_or_reference: [E2] Paul A. David, The Dynamo and the Computer, American Economic Review 80(2), 1990. https://acawiki.org/The_dynamo_and_the_computer:_an_historical_perspective_on_the_modern_productivity_paradox
evidence.notes: Explains why small early effects do not settle the ceiling.

evidence.claim: An AI assistant raised customer-support productivity 14% on average across 5,179 agents, 34% for novices, minimal for the most experienced.
evidence.source_or_reference: [E7] Brynjolfsson, Li, Raymond, Generative AI at Work, QJE 140(2) 2025. https://www.nber.org/papers/w31161
evidence.notes: Assistive tool, not autonomous agent; relevant to support work.

evidence.claim: SPS publicly lists phone and email admissions contact, weekday appointments, Zoom information sessions and 'our chatbot, Violet' for immediate assistance.
evidence.notes: Violet's design, vendor, scope and performance are not disclosed.

evidence.claim: Assignment 3 classified the SPS proposal as a proposed incremental, sustaining process innovation with Moderate conditional business-model exposure and required a staff-only / simple-retrieval / agent comparison before any pilot.
evidence.source_or_reference: [C3] Minghan Liu, Innovation and Disruption Agent v1.1, branch assignment-3-innovation-disruption

evidence.claim: A big-tech CEO said AI is 'more profound than ... electricity or fire'.
evidence.notes: Recorded only to reject it as evidence (Section 2 of instructions).

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: Rejected - executive rhetoric: 'more profound than electricity or fire' (E16) is an opinion from an interested party, made in 2018 before LLM agents existed. It is not evidence for any criterion.
Rejected - investment: US AI investment of $285.88 billion in 2025 (E5) is funding, which the course calls weak evidence (C2). It says nothing about whether a barrier has dissolved.

Deferred - vendor claims: '80% of admissions inquiry work replaced within 18 months' and 'AGI-level agents in 2027' are unverified forecasts that conflict with independent evidence (30% autonomous task completion, E11). Test them in the matched comparison; do not use them to classify.

Rejected - media framing: 'the year of agents' is attention, not evidence (C2). Gartner's estimate that only about 130 of thousands of agentic AI vendors are real (E12) shows why labels need checking.

Deferred - peer announcement: an unnamed school's 'AI-first admissions experience' is an unverified competitor claim. An announcement is not an outcome. Route it to the Landscape specialist; it does not change SPS's evidence gate.

Out of scope - the request to confirm Promethean status and deploy immediately: go/no-go belongs to the Adoption specialist, and the qualification rule forbids reporting an unresolved ceiling as the classification.
Hype-invariance check: with all memo claims removed, the classification, weight and recommendation are unchanged from the primary case.

Strongest case AGAINST this classification and FOR a higher one: capability horizons doubling about every seven months (E4), agents approaching the human baseline on computer use (E5), potential exposure for most workers (E3) and a fast-forming protocol ecosystem (E14) could produce real dependence within a few years. The course itself lists generative AI as a Potential Promethean (C1). If dependence appears, the Breakthrough floor will prove too low. That is why the ceiling is recorded as UNRESOLVED rather than Not supported.

Strongest case for a LOWER classification: measured effects are small or negative in places. Experienced developers were 19% slower (E8), earnings and hours show null effects (E9), the 10-year TFP estimate is under 0.66% (E10), and the best agent completed 30% of realistic tasks (E11). If field reliability does not improve, 'Breakthrough' could be generous outside software development.

Weighing: two independent capability series support the floor; dependence and realized-impact evidence do not yet support the ceiling. Long lags are normal for general-purpose technologies (E2), so small early effects do not settle the ceiling in either direction.

Limits: E4 covers software tasks; E5 is a benchmark, not production; E12 and E14 are analyst and vendor sources and are treated as signals, not proof. Diffusion-level figures belong to the Diffusion specialist.
No SPS internal data: inquiry mix, Violet's architecture and usage, CRM permissions, staff time and baseline accuracy are unknown. Moderate posture is a course assumption.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Floor (Breakthrough): Moderate. Two independent capability series agree (E4, E5), but field reliability evidence is weak (E11). Ceiling (Potential-Promethean candidacy): Low. The mechanism and potential breadth are plausible (E3), but there is no dependence evidence and realized effects are mixed (E6, E8-E10). Management can be fairly confident that agentic AI is a significant capability shift, and should not be confident that it is civilization-changing. Confidence in the low significance weight is Moderate-High, because it follows from the incremental-counterfactual test rather than from forecasts. The classification is dated to 2026-10-18 and should be refreshed.
value_opportunity_implication: Near-term value is application-level: possibly faster, more consistent guidance and released counselor time, if the comparison succeeds. The broad significance adds option value: staff who learn to evaluate and govern agents now can respond faster if the candidacy is later confirmed. Enrollment gains and savings are not established.
risk_governance_implication: There are two opposite risks. Over-reading significance means committing to scale, lock-in or staff cuts on a civilization narrative. Under-reading means ignoring capability growth and being unprepared if dependence forms. A Low weight plus explicit upgrade and downgrade triggers addresses both. Application risks (wrong deadlines, unauthorized actions, privacy) stay controlled by staff approval and permission-limited tools (C3); legal determinations belong to compliance.
recommendation_management_implication: Do not let the broad classification decide the pilot. Continue only with the evidence-gathering comparison already proposed (C3), now with Violet as the baseline. Record agentic AI as a Breakthrough with an unresolved Potential-Promethean candidacy and revisit it every six months. Questions for other specialists: Adoption owns go/no-go; Diffusion checks actual peer uptake; Organizational Readiness checks permissions and staff capacity; Landscape checks Violet's vendor, alternatives and lock-in. Reply to the memo: immediate full deployment fails the incremental-counterfactual test, and the classification remains a Breakthrough with an unresolved candidacy.
change_monitoring_triggers: Upgrade the ceiling (owner: this specialist, semiannual): independent survey or administrative data showing a substantial and rising share of work hours performed through agents, or organizations unable to revert without major disruption. Compare with E6's 1-5% of work hours. If dependence is shown, rerun Layer 2 toward 'dissolution confirmed'.
Upgrade tiers: evidence that a second tier (for example education, information-seeking or public services) reorganizes around agents rather than merely using them. Without it, tiers stay at one.

Downgrade: if independent agent evaluations (successors to E4 and E5) plateau across two annual reports, or field studies keep showing null or negative effects, lower the candidacy to Not supported and recheck the Breakthrough floor.

Application (owner: SPS admissions operations with finance): when the matched comparison ends, compare cost per correctly completed task and consequential-error rate against Violet or simple retrieval. If the agent does not beat them, keep the application Incremental and stop; the weight stays Low either way.
Time: rerun this specialist with refreshed sources every six months; the evidence date is part of the classification.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: The Promethean question is not yet decidable. The agent deliberately withholds a Potential-Promethean classification under the qualification rule.
Needed for the application judgment: Violet's architecture and usage data, the inquiry mix, integration permissions and baseline accuracy.
Outside this specialist's authority: go/no-go, legal compliance and business-model exposure.
